Tidy method for mysterycall_poisson_model objects

Source: R/poisson_model.R
tidy.mysterycall_poisson_model.Rd

Returns a broom-compatible tibble of fixed-effect incidence rate ratios (IRR) with Wald 95% CIs and p-values. Column names follow broom conventions so the result integrates with tidy workflows.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mysterycall_poisson_model'
tidy(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A mysterycall_poisson_model object returned by mysterycall_poisson_model().

...

Ignored; present for S3 consistency.

Value

A tibble::tibble() with one row per fixed-effect term and columns:

term

Coefficient name.

estimate

IRR (incidence rate ratio) on the exponentiated scale.

std.error

Standard error of the log-IRR.

statistic

z-statistic.

p.value

Two-tailed Wald p-value.

conf.low

Lower bound of 95% Wald CI for IRR.

conf.high

Upper bound of 95% Wald CI for IRR.

Examples

# \donttest{
fake_fit <- structure(
  list(irr_table = data.frame(
    term = "scenarioB", irr = 1.5, se = 0.15,
    z_value = 2.6, p_value = 0.009,
    ci_lower = 1.1, ci_upper = 2.0,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )),
  class = "mysterycall_poisson_model"
)
generics::tidy(fake_fit)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   term      estimate std.error statistic p.value conf.low conf.high
#>   <chr>        <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 scenarioB      1.5      0.15       2.6   0.009      1.1         2
# }
